conflicts.section: Known conflicts and their usual resolutions
rows: G23 reversal path vs at-least-once delivery
Idempotency key plus a compensating action. Where the effect is an irreversible external communication it can have neither — the only resolution is a pre-commit confirmation
G18 recall target vs an open-ended interpretive step where no golden dataset is constructible
Human sampling at a declared rate, plus an outcome assertion under G19. Record explicitly that the recall target is unobtainable rather than inventing a number
G19 independent monitoring vs a single-surface design
Always a boundary interface. No agent surface can monitor itself independently — this is structural, not a gap in the surfaces
Interactive latency vs G13 multi-source corroboration
Precompute the corroboration, or move the step to background and change the trigger modifier. Do not weaken corroboration to meet a latency target
G21 egress control vs business-owned change
Control at the template level rather than the prompt level. The business edits content within a structure engineering owns
G24 staged release vs an event-driven workload with no cohort
Rate limiting alone, with the partial coverage recorded. Staging requires a population to stage across
Permitted, gated on evaluation, with a review trigger. Lock-in accepted knowingly is different from lock-in arrived at
T3 platform orchestration vs G08 budgets
The obligation resolves to the EA block, since the platform owns control flow. Requires a named operator or it is unowned
